The harder you fight a problem, the bigger it gets.

Kevin explains that you become what you think about most of the time. If your mind stays on the problem, you give it more energy.

His point, in Earl Nightingale's words: what you resist persists. The way through is to welcome the challenge and overcome it instead of pushing back.

Which do you do more often, welcome a problem or push it away?

#ad #mindset #success #kevintrudeau

They can control everything except one thing.

Kevin points to Viktor Frankl's book Man's Search for Meaning. Frankl was held in a concentration camp, and he said they could take everything from him except his mind.

He controlled his thoughts, and that made his mind more powerful than anything done to him.

Kevin says he applied the same idea when he faced years in prison.

When did you last feel in control of your own thoughts?

#ad #mindset #confidence #kevintrudeau

What can a trained mind do in freezing cold?

Kevin describes photos of Tibetan monks meditating on snow in the Himalayas, doing the breath of fire. He says that within fifteen or twenty minutes the ice melts around them.

He also mentions Wim Hof, known as the Ice Man, who he says builds up heat in his body to handle freezing cold.

It is an example of how far training the mind may go.

What do you think the mind is capable of?
